item.title: Hegseth has remained defiant as Congress members deliberate articles of impeachment
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.
item.content:encoded: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.
item.dc:creator: David Folkenflik

item.title: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.
item.content:encoded:
House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

item.title: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.

(Image credit: Jim Watson)

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as their next leader
item.description: House GOP lawmakers have chosen Ohio's Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader, elevating a co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus to succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber's top Republican.
item.content:encoded: House GOP lawmakers have chosen Ohio's Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader, elevating a co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus to succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber's top Republican.

item.title: House GOP faults the federal government for failing to hold Epstein accountable
item.description: The House Oversight Committee has released a report into its investigation into sex-offender, Jeffrey Epstein. They faulted the federal government for not holding the financier accountable.

item.title: House set to vote to impeach Hegseth. And, SCOTUS allows border wall work to proceed
item.description: The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.
item.content:encoded:
The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.

(Image credit: Andrew Harnik)

item.title: The Democratic Party gained power across the country in the midterms. Now what?
item.description: Voters handed Democrats the keys to power across the country and expect them to drive in a different direction. Party leaders are now trying to figure out which way to go.
